title: Divisor extension implies punctured local parafactoriality
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be prime. Write $H(B)$ for its nonzero prime ideals having no prime strictly between them and $(0)$ [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group]. For $\mathfrak r\in H(B)$ let $v_{\mathfrak r}:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ be the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $B_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Assume first that every finite divisor $D=(d_{\mathfrak r})$ of $B$ which agrees with $\operatorname{div}(a)$ on the height-one primes contained in $\mathfrak p$, for some $a\in K^\times$, equals $\operatorname{div}(b)$ on all of $H(B)$ for some $b\in K^\times$. Assume in addition the following localization-stable divisor extension condition: for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and every finitely supported family of integers $(d_{\mathfrak r})_{\mathfrak r\in H(B),\,\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q}$, if for every prime $\mathfrak t\subseteq\mathfrak q$ with $\mathfrak t\subseteq\mathfrak p$ there exists $a_{\mathfrak t}\in K^\times$ such that $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a_{\mathfrak t})$ for every $\mathfrak r\in H(B)$ contained in $\mathfrak t$, then there exists $b\in K^\times$ such that $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(b)$ for every $\mathfrak r\in H(B)$ contained in $\mathfrak q$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$ with $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], set $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $P=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak qR\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. Then restriction $R\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ is an isomorphism, and every invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_P$.

source.place: EGA IV4 Corollary 21.13.15, implication (a) implies (b), with S={p}, and 21.13.8 for the meaning of local parafactoriality. The displayed hypothesis is the stronger global-principality form of (a), as in Remark 21.13.16. No Stacks tag states this criterion. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q$ as in the conclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$; it is local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Prime correspondence and iterated localization in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], together with [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], identify $H(R)$ with the $\mathfrak r\in H(B)$ contained in $\mathfrak q$. The local DVRs are the same subrings of $K$, so their normalized valuations agree. The maximal prime $\mathfrak qR$ is not height one, since its local ring is $R$ of dimension at least two. Thus every height-one point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ belongs to $P$.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain), and the prime-correspondence/local-ring arguments in the cited localization nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-local-depth-two] to $R$, with the Noetherian, local, normal-domain and dimension hypotheses verified in step 1. It gives depth at least two. Now [lem-sbc-depth-two-puncture-global-sections] says that restriction $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ is bijective. Under the canonical affine identification $R=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], this is exactly the displayed ring homomorphism. A bijective ring homomorphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal), S2 consequence; depth-two Hartogs as in the existing puncture-sections node and EGA IV4 21.13.4, 21.13.8(i).

proof.text: Let $L$ be an arbitrary invertible module on $P$. The open $P$ is nonempty: the prime $(0)$ differs from the maximal ideal, since $\dim R\ge2$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-open-line-weil-dictionary] to $(A,U,L)=(R,P,L)$. It supplies a finite divisor family $d$ on the height-one points of $P$, and local rational equations at every point of $P$. By step 1 this family is indexed by all $\mathfrak r\in H(B)$ contained in $\mathfrak q$, so it is an allowed input to the corrected extension hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 02SG, 0BE6 and 0BE8: associate the rational-section Weil cycle to L, as in EGA IV4 21.13.14.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak t\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak t\subseteq\mathfrak p$, then $\mathfrak t\ne\mathfrak q$: equality would contradict $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] therefore puts $\mathfrak tR$ in $P$. The local equation supplied in step 3 gives an $a_{\mathfrak t}$ with exactly the valuations required in the antecedent of the corrected hypothesis, using the identical DVRs of step 1. Apply that hypothesis to obtain one $b\in K^\times$ giving every coefficient of $d$. The final clause of [lem-sfb-normal-open-line-weil-dictionary] now yields $L\cong\mathcal O_P$. Since $L$ was arbitrary, this is the second conclusion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q131-7b40a7e84 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the new node and every cited statement in full; base statement taken from the Q87 snapshot. Sources: EGA IV4 21.13.8, 21.13.14 and 21.13.15 with their proofs, 21.13.16, 21.14.1 and 21.14.2 (translation markdown), and Stacks 0BE8 with its proof. The worker's E7 dispute is correct. EGA's 21.13.15(a) must hold on every open of X ('conditions are local'), not only for cycles on Spec B. I checked the counterexample myself. B=C[x,y,z,t]/(xy-z(z-t^2+1)) has singular locus exactly {p,q} (t=±1) and is normal. Cl(B)=Z·(x,z) because B[1/x] is a UFD and div x=P+Q. Both completions are xy=zw, and (x,z) generates their class group Z. So Cl(B)->Cl(B_p) is injective (the old hypothesis holds), while Pic of the punctured spectrum of B_q is Cl(B_q), which is nonzero, so the old conclusion fails. The corrected statement keeps both conclusions and adds the per-q local form of EGA's (a); it is true and not circular, and the item is not a target. Steps: (1) the localization nodes give R normal Noetherian local with H(R)={r in H(B): r⊆q} and identical DVRs; (2) normal-local-depth-two, then depth-two puncture sections, then R=Gamma gives the first conclusion; (3) P is nonempty and the dictionary applies with index set H(R); (4) t⊆p and t⊆q force t≠q, so the local equations exist, the hypothesis gives b, and the dictionary's iff gives L≅O_P. New node lem-sfb-normal-open-line-weil-dictionary: I proved it independently via a rational section and the Stacks 0BE8 argument. It is statement-only, all four search kinds are recorded, and it is not a duplicate: the regular-space dictionary needs regularity and parafactorial-principal-cycle-extension is the reverse direction. Batch 5: def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group is a general ring definition, not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, and the base item already cited it; accepted. Declared tool_uses (localization, depth-two, Hartogs, spec stalks) are generic and accepted.
